author: BrentDesk Staff
headline: Saudi Food Manufacturing opens in Jeddah with 1,000 exhibitors
deck: Saudi Food Manufacturing and the Saudi Food Show are built around scheduled buyer appointments and two awards schemes.
excerpt: Saudi Food Manufacturing and The Saudi Food Show organise their three days around a matchmaking programme and two awards schemes, with more than 1,000 exhibitors expected.
content:
Saudi Food Manufacturing and The Saudi Food Show open together at the Jeddah Superdome on 27 September, with the organiser giving combined figures of more than 1,000 exhibitors from over 95 countries, 100,000-plus products and 12,000 business meetings across three days.

The structure is built around those meetings. The TawaSul programme arranges buyer and supplier appointments in advance, the Saudifood Excellence Awards run across ten categories, and an innovation award sits on the manufacturing side. Together they define how the show is intended to be used.

Pre-arranged matchmaking is a mature exhibition format and it suits food procurement well. Buyers register sourcing requirements ahead of the event, suppliers register what they sell, and the organiser schedules meetings between matched pairs into timed slots. A buyer arrives with a diary rather than a floor plan, and a supplier receives qualified meetings rather than general stand traffic.

Food buying rewards that structure. It is repeat, relationship-driven business in which a buyer's requirement is usually specific — a category to fill, a specification to meet, a second source to establish — and the value of attending lies in finding the right counterparty. Twelve thousand scheduled meetings represents a substantial volume of that activity compressed into three days.

For exhibitors the format changes preparation. Meetings are allocated in advance, which means the qualification work happens before the doors open and the stand becomes a venue for conversations already scheduled rather than a device for attracting passing interest. Suppliers who complete their sourcing profiles thoroughly get better matches.

The awards carry more commercial weight in food than in many sectors. Retail buyers use category awards as a shortlist filter, and shelf-space decisions can follow, which makes ten categories across the food show a meaningful mechanism rather than a marketing exercise.

The exhibitor mix supports both halves. The food show side carries Almarai, NADEC, Americana, Arabian Mills, Arla, BRF, Lactalis and Zamil Food. The manufacturing side runs across ingredients, processing, packaging, supply chain solutions and control and automation, with Multivac, JBT-Marel, Provisur and ROVEMA among the named suppliers and a German pavilion of sixteen machinery builders with published stand numbers.

MODON is strategic partner to both shows. Durrah Sugar and First Mills hold gold sponsorships on the food show side with Arabian Mills and Snackland at silver, and ITEC takes silver on the manufacturing side.

Figures cited are the organiser's own projections.

The manufacturing side's German pavilion is the best-documented exhibitor block, with sixteen machinery builders confirmed down to hall and stand allocation, covering processing, packaging, refrigeration, fittings, automation and planning software.
